what_matters.head: All 35 names fell on Friday; the S&P 500 fund lost 3.6%, about 3.7 × its usual day, to its lowest since the 14 Apr report
what_matters.detail: Reuters says Anthropic's debut 'failed to catch fire' and deepened worries about the AI trade, and that neither it nor Nvidia's results eased concern about the cost of AI. The S&P 500 fell for a seventh session, its longest run since February 2020, and closed with the Dow more than 10% below its record. The Nasdaq fell 5.3%, its largest weekly drop since March 2020, and is now down for the year (Reuters). CNBC lists five forces behind the sell-off: Anthropic's IPO, Nvidia's troubles, a break below the 200-day average, inflation and the Fed, and slowing earnings growth (read through search results).

what_matters.head: Nvidia fell 14.0%, about 5.5 × its usual day, after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining its accounting (one report)
what_matters.detail: Reuters, citing two people briefed on the matter, said SEC enforcement staff are looking at potential accounting issues. It could not determine which issues or when the inquiry began, and notes that investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing. The Wall Street Journal had reported an SEC probe on Tuesday without its focus. Nvidia did not respond and the SEC declined to comment. The shares were down more than 6% before the report and about 13% after it (Reuters). Nvidia is down 22.9% in five sessions and 40.9% in a month.

what_matters.head: WeRide's Q3 revenue rose 88% to RMB 321.5M with a 43.0% gross margin; the shares fell 8.6%, about 2.2 × usual
what_matters.detail: Revenue was up 38.8% from Q2, and the gross margin compares with 32.9% a year earlier. The loss was RMB 310.0M, against 307.3M a year earlier, or RMB 0.96 per ADS. The company gave no financial forecast; its finance chief said it has more than four years of cash runway. Forbes ties Friday's fall to the slightly wider loss and does not mention the wider US sell-off that day.

after_data.lead: US futures and Asia on Monday
after_data.text: By 16:51 SGT on Monday Nasdaq 100 futures were up 3.3% and S&P 500 futures 2.5% (Reuters). Seoul's Kospi closed down 3.3% after falling as much as 5.8%, and Taiwan's index closed up about 2%; Japan was closed for a holiday (Al Jazeera). South Korea's finance minister repeated plans to stabilise the market if necessary, and Taiwan's regulator tightened short-selling rules (Reuters). Gold was up 2.1% at $3,606 and the 10-year yield up 5bp at 4.96% (Reuters). None of this is in Friday's US prices.

Out on Monday 23 Nov: MAS core inflation eased to 1.5% in the year to October, from 2.0% in September, and all-items inflation slowed to 1.9% from 2.2%. MAS puts the lower core figure down to lower inflation for services and for electricity and gas.

latest.tape_note: All 35 names fell in their latest session, and all 34 with a 50-day average are below it; more than half have been below in every report since 13 Oct. Fourteen names have an RSI under 30, against 18 in the 6 Nov report. The Nasdaq 100 fund fell 5.7% to its lowest since the 9 Apr report. The chip fund fell 10.6% on the day, 17.4% over five days and 22.2% in a month; Yahoo Finance says the chip sector was already on shaky ground after Jensen Huang's exit and concerns over AI financing. The 10-year yield fell 14bp to 4.91%, about 2.5 × usual; Reuters says government bonds rallied as investors sought safe havens. Gold fell 4.6%, about 2.9 × usual, to its lowest in the stored reports; Investing.com ties it to a sharp rise in expectations of a Fed rate rise and to traders selling gold to cover losses in AI stocks, on a day the 10-year yield fell.

vix_note.text: The VIX measures how big a swing in the S&P 500 traders are paying to protect against over the next 30 days, worked out from options prices; it rises when stocks fall fast and more protection is bought. It closed at 35.89 on Friday, up 26.2% on the day and 88.6% in a month, the highest in these daily reports, which start on 12 March. Reuters calls it the highest close since 7 April 2025 and reports it within its account of Friday's AI sell-off (item 1). No report found gives the VIX a separate cause.
